1.1.dialogue:
**You read — the harbour log, Wednesday night:**
> 20:40 — Lennox, creel boat, two crew, out to the Narrows. Due back 23:30.
> 23:30 — Not back.
> 00:15 — No answer on VHF. Tried three times.
> 05:50 — Boat drifted in against the pier. Empty.

**Brannan:** "I tried the radio when they were overdue. Read me the log, sergeant. How long had they been overdue when I tried?"
1.1.narration:
First light. You have been in Inverbrae six days and you have not yet seen the harbour empty. It is empty now. The Lennox boat has drifted in against the pier on its own, the mooring rope trailing in the water, the wheelhouse door open. Nobody aboard. In the stern, one yellow marker barrel lies on its side, chewed and split, as if a dog the size of a bus had worried it and let it go.

Fergus Brannan, the harbourmaster, is waiting for you with the night log open in his hands. He has not slept.
1.1.object: the yellow barrel in the stern
1.1.prompt: **Brannan:** "I tried the radio when they were overdue. Read me the log, sergeant. How long had they been overdue when I tried?"
1.1.right: Brannan tears it out and gives it to you. "Keep that. Somebody's going to ask."
1.1.title: THE DRIFTING BOAT
1.1.why: The boat was due at 23:30. The first radio call was at 00:15: FORTY-FIVE MINUTES later. Six hours and twenty minutes is the delay from 23:30 until the boat drifted in at 05:50.
1.1.wrong: "You've read it wrong. Read the next one right."

1.10.dialogue:
**You hear:**
**Menzies, to the crowd:** "Inverbrae has caught its monster!"
**Vass, to you:** "That's not it. Look at the colour. It ___ for a week, sergeant. It's been dead longer than the Lennox boat's been missing. They found it. They didn't catch it."
1.10.narration:
Midday, and the harbour is full of people again. Two brothers from Glasgow called Docherty have come up the coast in an orange RIB with a rifle and a net, and hanging from the harbour crane, grey and dripping, is a squid four metres long. Menzies is standing beside it in his best coat. Photographers. A cheer.

Vass walks under it with a tape measure and measures the beak. It is the size of her thumb. She comes back to you white with anger and speaks very quietly.
1.10.object: the squid on the harbour crane
1.10.prompt: **Vass, to you:** "That's not it. Look at the colour. It ___ for a week, sergeant. It's been dead longer than the Lennox boat's been missing. They found it. They didn't catch it."
1.10.right: Menzies catches your eye across the crowd and mouths one word: *smile*.
1.10.title: THE WRONG CATCH
1.10.why: a state that has lasted up to now takes HAS + BEEN + adjective + FOR a period. IS ... SINCE is a learner error for duration, and BEEN cannot be dropped after HAS.
1.10.wrong: Vass walks away. "I'll explain it to somebody who listens."

1.11a.object: the filleting knife under the lamp
1.11a.prompt: **Vass:** "Hold the torch steady. I've done this to a hundred of these and never one that smelled like this. Pass me the bucket. I ___ my dinner yet and I'd like to keep it that way."

1.11a.wrong: Vass: "You hold the torch. I'll do the English."

1.11b.dialogue:
**You hear:**
**Vass:** "He went out on Thursday. Nobody ___ him since. Nobody reported it because there was nobody to report it."
**You:** "Keep the torch on the hole."
1.11b.narration: Eleven o'clock, flat calm, no moon. You take the police RIB out past the moorings with Vass in the bow holding a torch. Dougie Ferrier fishes alone and lives alone, so nobody missed him. His boat, the *Kestrel*, is off the skerry, drifting, and the torch finds it before you do: the wheelhouse crushed inward like a paper cup, the hull holed below the waterline.
1.11b.object: the torch beam on the Kestrel's crushed wheelhouse
1.11b.prompt: **Vass:** "He went out on Thursday. Nobody ___ him since. Nobody reported it because there was nobody to report it."
1.11b.title: THE TORCH
1.11b.why: NOBODY is singular and takes HAS. SEEN is the participle; SAW is the Past Simple and never follows HAS.
1.11b.wrong: The torch shakes. That is not the grammar.

1.12a.dialogue:
**You hear:**
**Vass:** "Its last meal was mackerel and a bottle. The Lennox boat was taken on Wednesday night. Ewan's kayak was red, and there isn't a flake of red in here. This animal has been dead since before any of it happened."
**You:** "So what does its stomach prove?"
**Vass:** "You tell me. You're the police."
1.12a.narration: What comes out is mackerel, half of a plastic bottle and a lot of water. No rope. No paint. No cloth. Vass lays it all in a steel tray under the lamp and looks at it for a long time.
1.12a.object: the plastic bottle in the tray
1.12a.right: Vass: "Now we know what it isn't. That's more than the Provost knows."
1.12a.title: THE STOMACH
1.12a.why: no rope, no red paint, and it has been dead since before Wednesday. It could not have taken the boat or the kayak.
1.12a.wrong: Vass stops explaining things to you.

1.12b.dialogue:
**You hear:**
**Vass:** "A propeller cuts. A rock tears. Look at the edges. This is round, forty centimetres across, and every plank is bent inwards. This was pushed. Something outside the boat pushed the hull in."

Something moves under the crushed wheelhouse. You do not wait to see what.

**Vass, as you open the throttle:** "Well? What made the hole?"
1.12b.narration: Vass leans over and pulls a black curved shard out of the planking beside the hole. She holds it against the ring in the jar. Same curve, same edge. Then she puts the torch through the hole and you both look.
1.12b.object: the round hole in the hull, lit from inside
options: The skerry tore it open from below
1.12b.prompt: **Vass, as you open the throttle:** "Well? What made the hole?"
1.12b.right: Vass puts the shard in her pocket. "Two beaks, one animal."
1.12b.title: THE HOLE
1.12b.why: round, planks bent inward, pushed from outside. A propeller would cut and a rock would tear; Vass rules out both.

**Brannan:** "Marshal, say again. How many in the water?"
**Weir:** "Six. Six children, two boats, and me. Get the boats in. Get the —"

**Brannan, running beside you:** "How many people are in the water, sergeant, and how many of them are children?"

Regatta Sunday, the big race, and Menzies has refused to cancel it. You have the police RIB out, the lifeboat on standby and Tulloch's *Kittiwake* sitting at the harbour mouth because he has decided to be there. In the inner bay the junior fleet is racing in white dinghies. Your daughter Kirsty is twelve, and she is in one of them.

At half past eleven two boys in a small motorboat tow a black tarpaulin past the beach. The wet sheet rises and falls behind them, and four hundred people scream and run. You are still shouting at the boys when the radio goes.

Old Mrs Rennie, who has lived above the harbour for eighty years, tells you it has not been rung since the *Ossian* went down, and that was when you were a child. Brannan has the rope in his hand and he is looking at you, because you are the police and it is your call.

Behind him the village has started to come down the hill. Nobody has said the word yet.

**You:** "Two men haven't come home."
**Menzies:** "Two men had an accident. It happens on a coast. Tell me, in your career, ___ a harbour in August? No. Because nobody has."

1.4.dialogue:
**You hear — the shipping forecast, issued 17:05 Thursday:**
> "Malin, Hebrides. Southwesterly 3 or 4, increasing 5 to 7 later. Slight
> or moderate, becoming rough later. Fair. Good."
> "Inshore, Ardnamurchan Point to Mull of Kintyre. Southwesterly 3 or 4,
> increasing 5 to 7 later. Smooth or slight, becoming moderate."

**Brannan:** "The regatta starts at ten tomorrow morning. If the forecast is right about LATER, what's the earliest the wind can get up to force 7?"
1.4.narration: Brannan's office is a wooden hut at the end of the pier with a kettle, a barometer and a radio that has been on since 1987. At five past five he turns it up. He tells you the rules before it starts: IMMINENT means inside six hours, SOON means six to twelve, LATER means more than twelve, and the clock starts from the time the forecast is issued.
1.4.object: the radio on the harbourmaster's desk
options: At ten tomorrow, when the racing starts
1.4.prompt: **Brannan:** "The regatta starts at ten tomorrow morning. If the forecast is right about LATER, what's the earliest the wind can get up to force 7?"
1.4.right: Brannan writes it out in pencil and hands it over. "Show him that. He won't read it, but show him."
1.4.title: THE FORECAST
1.4.why: LATER means more than twelve hours after the time of issue. Twelve hours after 17:05 is 05:05 on Friday. It can come after that; nothing in the forecast says it will wait for the racing.
1.4.wrong: "You've got the words the wrong way round, and out there that's the difference between a boat and no boat."

You are on the pier with the radio Menzies has paid for. You have been watching the water for an hour and you have not seen a single fish jump. The gulls have gone somewhere else.

The ball floats back to the slip on its own. The collie does not.

1.9.dialogue:
**You hear:**

3.9.dialogue:
**You hear — Tulloch, in your head, from Sunday:** "The gun's got one shot. The line runs to the barrel. Don't fire till you can see the eye, and don't fire from above, because the head's armoured. Fire level, into the mouth."

**The question is Tulloch's, and it is the only one that matters:** "When do you fire?"

prologue.narration:
Ten o'clock, and the light has almost gone. Davie Lennox and his nephew Tam are hauling creels at the mouth of the Narrows, where the deep water starts. Tam has been fishing with his uncle for three summers and he knows the sounds of the boat by heart: the winch, the creel on the rail, the gulls.

Tonight there are no gulls.

"Davie. Where have the birds gone?"

Davie doesn't answer. The rope on the winch has gone tight. Not creel-tight. Tight like something has taken hold of it and is pulling it down, slowly, with all the time in the world. The stern dips. The yellow marker barrel rolls across the deck.

"Cut it," says Davie. "Cut the rope."

Tam has the knife in his hand when the water beside the boat goes white.
prologue.object: the yellow barrel on the deck
prologue.title: THE NARROWS
